title: Executables and file names
note: Names of executables found inside the selected instance, and file-name hints. A name alone is never more than suspicious.

rules.name: Auto-clicker executed
rules.description: An executable whose name identifies it as an auto-clicker is stored inside the Minecraft instance. Auto-clickers automate attacks (CPS manipulation).
rules.falsePositives: Auto-clickers have non-gaming uses (accessibility, idle games). Execution time must be correlated with the game session.
rules.limitations: Matched against executables stored inside the selected instance. Names are user-controlled; a renamed tool will not match, but every executable in the instance is also string-scanned.

rules.name: DLL injector executed
rules.description: An executable named like a DLL injector is stored inside the Minecraft instance. Injectors are used to load ghost clients into the game process.
rules.falsePositives: Some modding tools for other games are named "injector".
rules.limitations: Matched against executables stored inside the selected instance. Names are user-controlled; a renamed tool will not match, but every executable in the instance is also string-scanned.

rules.name: Memory editor executed (Cheat Engine)
rules.description: Cheat Engine, a memory scanner/editor, is stored inside the Minecraft instance.
rules.falsePositives: Cheat Engine is commonly used for singleplayer games and learning.
rules.limitations: Matched against executables stored inside the selected instance. Names are user-controlled; a renamed tool will not match, but every executable in the instance is also string-scanned.

rules.name: Process manipulation tool executed
rules.description: Process Hacker / System Informer is stored inside the Minecraft instance. These tools can terminate processes, edit memory strings and unload modules.
rules.limitations: Matched against executables stored inside the selected instance. Names are user-controlled; a renamed tool will not match, but every executable in the instance is also string-scanned.

rules.name: Secure-delete tool executed
rules.description: A secure file deletion tool is stored inside the Minecraft instance. Secure deletion prevents recovery of files that were removed.
rules.limitations: Matched against executables stored inside the selected instance. Names are user-controlled; a renamed tool will not match, but every executable in the instance is also string-scanned.

rules.name: Macro automation runtime executed (AutoHotkey)
rules.description: AutoHotkey is stored inside the Minecraft instance. AutoHotkey scripts can implement clicker or macro behaviour.
rules.falsePositives: AutoHotkey is a very common productivity tool.
rules.limitations: Matched against executables stored inside the selected instance. Names are user-controlled; a renamed tool will not match, but every executable in the instance is also string-scanned.

rules.name: File named after a known cheat client
rules.description: A Java archive, executable or library is named after a known cheat client.
rules.falsePositives: File names are user-controlled; a file may be mis-named, an installer, or unrelated. A name alone never confirms a client.
rules.limitations: Renamed clients will not match. The file content is analysed separately when it still exists.

rules.name: JNativeHook native library extracted
rules.description: The JNativeHook native library was extracted to a temporary folder. JNativeHook gives Java programs global mouse/keyboard hooks and is used by Java auto-clickers.
rules.falsePositives: Legitimate Java applications (hotkey tools, overlays) also use JNativeHook.
rules.limitations: Only observed in temporary folders; the extracting program is not identified.
